title: そんなに — “that much / so ～”
summary: An adverb for “that much / so” about a degree the listener or topic involves. With a negative, it means “not so ～”.

patterns.gloss: そんなに + adjective / verb (そんなに怒っている)

body.p: It points to the degree of something the listener said or is doing: そんなに急がなくてもいい, そんなに難しくない.
Use こんなに for what is close to the speaker and あんなに for things far from both. With a negative it is close to あまり～ない.

examples.ja: そんなに急（いそ）がなくてもいいですよ。
examples.romaji: Sonna ni isoganakute mo ii desu yo.
examples.tr: You don't have to hurry so much.

examples.ja: この問題（もんだい）はそんなに難（むずか）しくない。
examples.romaji: Kono mondai wa sonna ni muzukashikunai.

examples.ja: どうしてそんなに怒（おこ）っているの。
examples.romaji: Dōshite sonna ni okotte iru no.

pitfalls: With a negative it means “not so ～”.
For something close to yourself use こんなに.
